description: imbh — embeddable observability database as a Docker log driver

env.name: IMBH_DOCKER_PLUGIN_SOCKET
env.description: Where imbhd serves the log-driver plugin API. Must match interface.socket.

env.name: IMBH_LISTEN_ADDR
env.description: OTLP/HTTP ingest + SQL query endpoint. Defaults to the docker0 bridge address, which containers can reach and the LAN cannot; build.sh replaces it with the address this daemon actually uses. Set to the empty string to open no TCP port at all.

env.name: IMBH_GRPC_LISTEN_ADDR
env.description: OTLP/gRPC ingest (the default transport for most OTel SDKs), same addressing rules as IMBH_LISTEN_ADDR. Empty disables it.

env.name: IMBH_FLUSH
env.description: When buffered rows are sealed into Parquet segments (which is also what lets the WAL be reclaimed). Triggers OR together: interval=5s, buffer=16MiB, rows=50000, wal=64MiB, idle=2s, tick=250ms. `manual` seals only on POST /admin/flush and shutdown.

env.name: IMBH_MAINTENANCE_INTERVAL
env.description: How often the retention policy is applied.

env.name: IMBH_HEADER_TIMEOUT
env.description: Total time an HTTP client gets to deliver a request line and headers before it is answered 408 and disconnected. Bounds what one idle client can hold, since the server is thread-per-connection. `0` disables it.

env.name: IMBH_BODY_TIMEOUT
env.description: How long a single read of an HTTP request body -- or a single write of a response -- may stall. Per read, not per request, so a large slow upload is fine as long as it keeps making progress. `0` disables it.

env.name: IMBH_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT
env.description: On SIGTERM (a `docker plugin disable`), how long in-flight requests and container lines get to finish before the buffer is sealed and the process exits. `0` does not wait. Keep it under the daemon's own stop grace.

env.name: RUST_LOG
env.description: Log filter for imbhd's own diagnostics. Output goes to the Docker daemon log.

mounts.name: data
mounts.description: Host directory holding the imbh database. Set with: docker plugin set <plugin> data.source=/path
